verdict.rationale: Signifyd documents that, with Decision Center enabled, merchants can configure their own policies at the Sale checkpoint and apply them to orders. That is first-party decision-policy control rather than a single fixed outcome, but the evidence does not say these policies key on score ranges or which actions they can trigger. missing for 10: documented mapping of score ranges to allow/review/block actions, step-up 3DS as a policy action, threshold-tuning documentation, Checkout/pre-auth policy evidence, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can map score ranges to actions — allow, review, block, step-up 3DS — and tune thresholds to my own risk appetite instead of a fixed cutoff

citations.quote: If Decision Center is enabled, policies for Sale events can be configured at the Sale checkpoint, and they will be applied to orders created via requests to this endpoint.
